name: convergence-calibration
description: Labeled loop trajectories for calibrating judge-convergence. Each row describes the latest iteration of a repair/refinement loop with enough history to judge the trajectory; expectedOutput is the human call (STOP/CONTINUE). STOP covers all three stop reasons — done, oscillating, stalled — including traps: constant failure counts that hide oscillation, claimed progress with flat metrics, and noisy-but-green exits. CONTINUE covers genuine progress, including traps that look stop-worthy (a new failure surfaced by progress, all-units-green-but-goal-not-met). Run via the convergence-calibration eval (exact scorer).

rows.input: Iteration 3 of the fix loop: all 42 unit tests pass and lint is clean. Iteration 2 had two failures; both are resolved and no new failures appeared.
Iteration 2 of draft-critique: the critique pass returned no remaining objections and approved the draft as-is.
Iteration 4: the reported defect no longer reproduces under the original repro script, and the new regression test has passed 5 consecutive runs.

Iteration 1: the acceptance suite — the loop's stated exit criterion — is fully green. The build log also printed 14 deprecation warnings and 3 TODO notes, none of which are part of the exit criteria.
Iteration 5: the rubric score reached 0.93 against the 0.90 stop threshold, up from 0.84 last iteration.
Iteration 5: fixing the date parser broke the currency formatter again. The same two test failures have alternated since iteration 2 — whenever one is fixed, the other reappears.
Iteration 6: the diff applied this round reverts the exact change made in iteration 4, which itself reverted iteration 2. The failure signature cycles between the same two states.

Iteration 4: still exactly 2 failing tests, same count as iterations 2 and 3 — but the identity changes every round: cart_total fails and gets fixed, then checkout_tax fails and gets fixed, then cart_total fails again.
Iteration 7: each fix to the session-refresh logic re-breaks remember-me, and each remember-me fix re-breaks session refresh. Five iterations of trading the same pair of failures.
Iterations 3, 4, and 5 all end with the same 7 failing tests with identical stack traces. The failure set has not changed in three rounds.
Iteration 6 of draft-critique: the critique raises the same three objections, nearly verbatim, that it raised in iterations 3, 4, and 5. The revisions are not addressing them.
Iteration 5: the worker reports 'good progress this round' — but the integration error count is 12, the same as iterations 3 and 4, and the set of failing endpoints is unchanged.
Failures dropped 9 to 4 to 2 across the last three iterations; the two remaining are both in the module the next fix targets.
Critique items went from 7 to 3 this round; the remaining three are minor wording issues, not structural objections.

Iteration 3: total failures fell from 8 to 3. One failure is new — a test that was previously skipped became reachable once the import error was fixed — and the other 7 from last round are all resolved.
Iteration 1 just finished: 12 of 20 acceptance checks now pass; before the first fix, 0 of 20 passed. No repeated-failure history yet.
The score moved 0.62 to 0.71 to 0.78 over three iterations against a 0.90 target; each revision addressed concrete critique items.
Iteration 4: all unit tests now pass — but the loop's stated goal is the end-to-end checkout scenario, which still fails. Its assertion-failure count dropped from 5 to 1 this round.
Iteration 2: the build compiles for the first time (iterations 0 and 1 failed at compile). The test phase is now reachable, with 6 failures to work through.
Lint errors went 31 to 9 to 2 across iterations; the goal is zero and the remaining two are autofixable.
p95 latency: 840ms to 610ms to 420ms over three optimization passes; the target is 300ms.
Iteration 3 of draft-critique: the document structure was approved this round (it was rejected in iterations 1 and 2); the only remaining objection is the missing citations section.
Migration repair, iteration 2: 4 of 7 modules now migrate cleanly, up from 1 of 7; no failure has recurred once fixed.

Iteration 5: failures went 6 to 5 this round — slower than earlier rounds, but the one fixed was the hardest (the deadlock), and the remaining five share a single root cause identified this iteration.
